checks: For each fixed nonvertical normal the through-mark threshold is convex by concavity of f and ε≥0. A threshold superlevel of a nonincreasing tail is an initial interval, also for the closed pure-base step tail. Therefore every integer-base combination of deepest marks is feasible in C, sampled, and deepest.

At the attained common cap the threshold derivative −S_0 is strictly negative, so every greater threshold has mass strictly below Q, by local differentiation and global monotonicity. All input thresholds are at most the common threshold, while their weighted mean is at least that threshold. Positive coefficients force equality for each input.

Varying a in both signs at each input preserves u and the width, changes the threshold by v·p_i, and gives exactly the common weighted slab base mean. The positive denominator forces all p_i to coincide. Choosing one mark per base gives both hull-lattice equality and extremality; the integer midpoint of a same-parity pair gives the stated count, including rank-zero bases.

At fixed nonzero u the two ramp kink levels cut each measured fiber in null hyperplanes, and the bounded local difference quotients converge elsewhere. The derivative integrands converge off the limiting kink planes, so the first derivatives are continuous. With a C¹ norm off zero this works in u as well. The original §7 claim is properly restricted for nonsmooth norms.
The frozen source locators §§2–5 and §7 match the threshold propagation, arbitrary positive combination, centroid, and ramp arguments.

overlap.comparison: Proves parity separation via the same centroid argument for a midpoint of a same-parity pair using a differentiable CDF. This draft treats every integer-base positive combination, obtains lattice-hull and vertex assertions, and handles the ramp and the needed regularity distinction.

Its unsmoothed one-integer-coordinate interpolation needs proper actual source traces and a trimmed section-mean argument. It does not give a common smoothed slab or the arbitrary-rank deepest-base conclusion.

readability: The convex threshold argument is carried out on C before restricting to integer bases. No joint u derivative is required for base-normal stationarity.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: Positive mass in one attaining slab makes every integer-base interpolation of deepest marks share a single source base and gives the stated lattice and vertex conclusions.
